subject.title: Context pruning mode 'off' not preventing compactions (Anthropic API key, cache-ttl smart defaults)

question: Should OpenClaw support a hard-limit-only or fully-off automatic compaction mode, and should persisted compaction entries carry a closed trigger reason?
rationale: Current main already honors pruning off, but changing compaction disable semantics and persisted transcript metadata is a safety/config contract decision.

options.title: Define Hard-Limit Semantics
options.body: Add an approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold or safeguard compaction, plus trigger metadata, docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep Current Policy
options.body: Treat automatic compaction as always available by design and narrow work to verified false low-context triggers and clearer docs.

options.title: Wait For Live Anthropic Proof
options.body: Require current-main Anthropic API-key reproduction before accepting new compaction semantics beyond the related low-context reports.

recommendation.title: Define Hard-Limit Semantics
recommendation.body: Add an approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold or safeguard compaction, plus trigger metadata, docs, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent compaction reserve capping and current-line config/runtime blame make him the best available owner for the compaction safety contract choice.
